title: UI skin
description: ui/skins/<id>/skin.yaml of any pack: the look of every screen of the UI, which the player picks with the ui_skin setting. A skin only changes the look: the documents keep their element ids, scripts and commands (docs/architecture/ui.md).

menuLayout.description: How the screen is laid out: as the modern look's, or as the original game's.

pictureLayout.description: Where the title's picture and the boxes over it go in a wide window: the style sheet's places (modern), or the original's places across the widened picture while «widescreen pictures» is on (original).

barsLayout.description: How the field HUD's bars fill: smoothly (continuous), or in the original game's 25 steps (pips).

pagesLayout.description: How the partner menu's status, tech and item pages are drawn: in the menu's panel (modern), as the original game's full screens (original), or with the status and the techniques on one page, no tab row and Cancel closing back to the pause menu (compact).

headingLayout.description: Whether the save machine's heading stays over its save question: only over the register and the slots, as in the original game (original), or over the question too (always).

poolLayout.description: What the partner menu's HP and MP bars fill with: the maximum against the cap, as the original game (maximum), or the amount left over the maximum (current).

tabsLayout.description: Which tabs the pause menu's player page offers in the original layout: all of them (all), or the profile, the chart and the city only, walked with the tab keys too and with a Back tab (minimal).

medalsLayout.description: Where the pause menu's player page shows the medals in the original layout: on a page of their own (page), or in a box on the profile, without their tab (profile).

boxLayout.description: How the screen's boxes open: at once (modern), or growing from a grey outline as in the original game.

assetId.description: An asset id: the path without its extension.

id.description: The skin's id: the name of its folder under ui/skins/.

name.description: The text key of the name the menus show, such as ui_skin.<id> for the game pack's skins; a mod keeps its keys in a localization file of its own.

extends.description: The id of a skin this one adds to: its sheets apply first, so this skin's rules win.

cursor.description: The image this skin installs as the system mouse cursor while it is the one on screen. Written relative to the skin's own folder (`cursor: cursor` reads as `ui/skins/<id>/cursor`). The nearest skin in the chain that names one wins; a skin that does not leaves the system arrow.

cursor_hotspot.description: The click point of the cursor image, [x, y] in pixels of the image from its top-left corner. (0, 0) when not given.

theme.description: RCSS style sheets for every document, before each screen's styles.

screens.description: The look of each screen, by the name the game loads its document under (hud, main_menu, pause_menu, partner_menu, battle).

styles.description: RCSS style sheets for the screen, in order.

document.description: An RML document that replaces the screen's own: the same element ids and scripts, laid out another way.

document_classes.description: Classes the skin puts on elements of the documents every skin shares, by the name the game loads the document under, then by element id; a switch takes them off again. The documents' scripts read them (for example pips on the field HUD's bars) and must not toggle them. An id the document lacks, or a document the game does not load, is a warning.

layout.description: Layout options the screens' scripts read with ui.layout(option), by the name the game loads the document under; the body of the document also gets the class layout-<option>-<value>. A skin that extends another inherits the options it does not set.

sprite_sheets.description: Sprite sheets the style sheets use (RCSS @spritesheet), measured in the pixels of the original image.

name.description: The sprite sheet's name in RCSS.

image.description: The image's asset id; any file type the packs provide (PNG, KTX2).

palette.description: A palette of the indexed image's metadata (<image>_meta.yaml) to draw it with.

original_size.description: The image's size in original pixels, [width, height]; a larger image is an upscaled copy and the sprites grow with it.

dp_per_pixel.description: How many dp an original pixel covers (3 draws the original's 240 lines over the UI's 720 dp).

upscale.description: smooth: drawn smoothed by the texture upscaler when the player's texture filter is the upscaler (a picture whose curves and cut-out edges show stairs as pixel art).

mirror_sides.description: [left, right]: columns of the game's own image mirrored past its left and right edges (the image reference's mirror_left and mirror_right), so a picture that fills a wider window carries on past its edges; original_size counts them.

sprites.description: Each sprite's rectangle in original pixels: [x, y, width, height].
